title: Amalickiah Found Dead
summary: On the first morning of the first month, the Lamanites find Amalickiah dead in his tent and see that Teancum is ready to give them battle. Afraid, they abandon their plan to march northward and retreat into Mulek, seeking protection in its fortifications.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites found Amalickiah dead in his own tent and saw that Teancum was ready to give them battle that day.
The Lamanites were afraid, abandoned their plan to march northward, and retreated with their army into Mulek for protection in its fortifications.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites can see Amalickiah inside his tent.
unspecified_visual_details: The tent’s design, the army’s appearance, and the fortifications’ construction are unspecified.

narration.text: they found Amalickiah was dead in his own tent; and they also saw that Teancum was ready to give them battle on that day.

prohibited_inventions: Do not state or depict who killed Amalickiah or how he died; these verses do not say.

title: Ammoron Takes the Throne
summary: Ammoron is appointed king and commands his people to hold the cities they have taken.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah’s brother Ammoron was appointed king in his stead.
Ammoron commanded his people to maintain the cities they had taken, at the cost of much bloodshed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammoron can be shown addressing his people as their newly appointed king.
unspecified_visual_details: The place of appointment, ceremony, clothing, and manner of address are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a coronation or invent Ammoron’s exact words.

title: Teancum Strengthens His Position
summary: Seeing the Lamanites’ numbers and strongholds, Teancum does not attack. He prepares defenses until Moroni sends reinforcements.

explicit_facts.text: Teancum judged an attack on the Lamanites in their forts unwise because of their numbers and determination to hold their cities.
Teancum kept his men around him, raised walls, and prepared places of resort while preparing to defend himself.
He continued preparing until Moroni sent many men to strengthen his army.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephite soldiers can be shown raising defensive walls.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact site, construction methods, and appearance of the defenses are not specified.

narration.text: he kept his men round about

prohibited_inventions: Do not show an attack on the Lamanite forts in this moment.

title: Moroni’s Orders
summary: Moroni sends orders to an unnamed recipient to retain prisoners for ransom, fortify Bountiful and secure the narrow pass. He also urges the recipient to maintain that quarter, seek opportunities against the Lamanites, recover captured cities if possible, and strengthen cities not yet captured.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni orders the recipient to retain prisoners of the Lamanites as ransom for those the Lamanites had taken.
Moroni orders the recipient to fortify the land Bountiful and secure the narrow pass into the land northward.
Moroni asks the recipient to maintain that quarter, seek opportunities against the Lamanites, recover captured cities if possible, and strengthen cities not captured.

unspecified_visual_details: The recipient’s identity and appearance are not stated.
The location and means of sending the orders are not stated.

he should fortify the land Bountiful, and secure the narrow pass

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are orders and desired actions; the verses do not say they were carried out.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the recipient or invent a messenger, written letter, delivery method, or prisoners present in the scene.
Do not depict the requested fortifications, fighting, or recovery of cities as completed events.

title: Ammoron Marches West
summary: Moroni says he cannot come because the Lamanites are at the west border. Ammoron has gathered a large force and marches there, while forces left behind are ordered to harass Nephites by the east sea. The Nephites are in dangerous circumstances at the end of the twenty-sixth year.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says the Lamanites are at the west border and that he is going against them, so he cannot come to Teancum.
Ammoron leaves Zarahemla, informs the queen of his brother’s death, gathers many men, and marches against the Nephites at the west sea border.
Ammoron intends to draw away Nephite forces in the west while ordering forces left behind to harass Nephites by the east sea and take their lands where possible.
The Nephites are in dangerous circumstances at the end of the twenty-sixth year.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammoron and his gathered force can be shown marching toward the west sea border.
unspecified_visual_details: The queen’s appearance and location, and the exact positions of forces on both borders, are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the queen or invent her response; she is only mentioned.

title: Teancum Returns to Bountiful
summary: In the twenty-seventh year, Moroni orders an attack on Mulek. Teancum prepares to march but judges the fortified Lamanites impossible to overpower, abandons the attack, and returns to Bountiful to await Moroni.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni has established armies to protect the south and west borders and begun marching toward Bountiful to help Teancum retake lost cities.
Teancum receives orders to attack Mulek and retake it if possible.
Teancum prepares to attack but decides he cannot overpower the Lamanites in their fortifications; he returns to Bountiful to await Moroni and reinforcements.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The scene may show Teancum’s army turning back toward Bountiful after preparing to attack.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise route and the appearance of the fortifications are unspecified.

narration.text: returned again to the city Bountiful

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle at Mulek in this scene.

title: Moroni Arrives at Bountiful
summary: Moroni arrives with his army at the land of Bountiful late in the twenty-seventh year.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni arrives with his army at Bountiful late in the twenty-seventh year.

title: Council of War
summary: At the beginning of the twenty-eighth year, Moroni, Teancum, and chief captains hold a council about drawing the Lamanites out of their strongholds and retaking Mulek.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni, Teancum, and many chief captains hold a council of war to consider how to bring the Lamanites out to battle or lure them from their strongholds and retake Mulek.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The leaders can be shown gathered in council.
unspecified_visual_details: The council’s exact place and the details of its discussion are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or the specific plan here; the plan is described in later verses.

title: Jacob Does Not Come Out
summary: Embassies are sent to Jacob, leader of the Lamanite army protecting Mulek, asking him to meet them with his armies on the plains between the two cities. Jacob does not come out. Moroni then resolves to decoy the Lamanites from their strongholds.

explicit_facts.text: Embassies are sent to Jacob, leader of the Lamanite army protecting Mulek, asking him to meet them with his armies on the plains between the two cities.
Jacob is a Zoramite and does not come out with his army to meet them.
Moroni resolves to decoy the Lamanites out of their strongholds.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The embassies may be shown traveling toward the Lamanite army; no exchange with Jacob is specified.
Jacob’s refusal and Moroni’s subsequent decision should not be depicted as simultaneous.
unspecified_visual_details: The embassies’ composition, appearance, and route are unspecified.
The other city and the precise appearance of the strongholds are unspecified.

narration.text: But behold, Jacob, who was a Zoramite, would not come out with his army to meet them upon the plains.
he resolved upon a plan that he might decoy the Lamanites out of their strongholds.

title: The Decoy Is Set
summary: Teancum takes a small force near the seashore while Moroni’s army marches by night through the wilderness west of Mulek. The next day, Lamanite guards discover Teancum and report to Jacob.

explicit_facts.text: Teancum takes a small number of men near the seashore; Moroni and his army march at night through the wilderness west of Mulek.
The following day Lamanite guards discover Teancum and report to their leader Jacob.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The night march and the guards’ discovery can be conveyed as separate visual elements within the unfolding maneuver.
unspecified_visual_details: The seashore’s appearance and the guards’ exact means of reporting are unspecified.

title: Teancum Draws Them Out
summary: The Lamanite army marches against Teancum, who retreats north along the seashore. Believing he is fleeing, the Lamanites pursue; Moroni sends part of his army into Mulek to seize it.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites march against Teancum, expecting their numbers to overwhelm his smaller force; Teancum retreats north by the seashore.
The Lamanites pursue Teancum, while Moroni orders part of his army to enter Mulek and take possession of it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Teancum’s force can be shown retreating while the Lamanites pursue, with Moroni’s force moving toward Mulek.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact distance between the seashore and Mulek is unspecified.

title: Moroni Takes Mulek
summary: Moroni’s soldiers take Mulek, killing those left to protect it who refuse to surrender their weapons. Moroni holds the city with part of his army and takes the rest to meet the returning Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni’s soldiers take Mulek and kill its remaining defenders who will not yield their weapons.
Moroni holds Mulek with part of his army and marches with the rest to meet the Lamanites returning from pursuit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The defenders may be shown surrendering or resisting as Moroni’s soldiers take the city.

title: Lehi Blocks the Pursuit
summary: The Lamanites pursue Teancum near Bountiful, where Lehi and a small force meet them. The Lamanite captains flee in confusion, fearing they will lose Mulek before Lehi catches them; they do not know Moroni is behind them. Lehi waits for them to meet Moroni.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites pursue Teancum near Bountiful and meet Lehi with a small army left to protect the city.
The Lamanite chief captains flee in confusion, fearing they might not reach Mulek before Lehi overtakes them; they are weary, while Lehi’s men are fresh.
The Lamanites do not know Moroni is behind them and fear only Lehi and his men.
Lehi does not intend to overtake them until they meet Moroni and his army.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi’s fresh force can be shown confronting the weary Lamanites near Bountiful.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain and distance to Mulek are unspecified.

title: The Lamanites Are Surrounded
summary: Before the Lamanites retreat far, Moroni’s men and Lehi’s men surround them from opposite sides. Moroni commands his men to attack until the Lamanites surrender their weapons.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites surround the Lamanites, with Moroni’s men on one side and Lehi’s on the other; the Nephites are fresh and the Lamanites weary.
Moroni commands his men to attack until the Lamanites give up their weapons.

title: Jacob Leads the Lamanites
summary: Jacob leads the Lamanites in a furious attack against Moroni, determined to cut through to Mulek. Moroni’s men hold their ground. Fighting erupts on both sides; many are slain, Moroni is wounded, and Jacob is killed.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob leads the Lamanites with exceeding fury against Moroni.
Jacob is determined to kill Moroni’s men and cut through to Mulek, but Moroni’s men do not give way.
The armies fight on both sides; many are slain, Moroni is wounded, and Jacob is killed.

title: The Lamanites Surrender
summary: Lehi presses the Lamanite rear, and many surrender their weapons. Moroni offers to spare the Lamanites who surrender. Their surviving captains throw down their weapons and order their men to do likewise; those who refuse are bound, disarmed, and marched with the others into Bountiful. The prisoners outnumber those slain on both sides.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi presses the Lamanites’ rear; those there surrender their weapons, while the confused remainder do not know where to go or strike.
Moroni offers to spare the Lamanites if they surrender their weapons.
The surviving Lamanite chief captains throw down their weapons at Moroni’s feet and command their men to do likewise.
Those who refuse to surrender are taken and bound, disarmed, and compelled to march into Bountiful with their brethren.
The number of prisoners exceeds the number slain on both sides.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The surrendering captains can be shown laying weapons at Moroni’s feet; refusing Lamanites can be shown bound and disarmed.
